Connectors

3,000+ apps, with your access. Never more.

Connect the tools you already use and Maia works in them as you. Reads run straight through. Risky writes wait for a yes.

Connect once, for yourself

Each person connects their own apps. Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Linear, GitHub, Notion, HubSpot, Jira, and a catalog you can search. Maia acts in each app as the person who asked, and a channel coworker uses the apps it was set up with.

There is no shared service account. No admin connects an app on your behalf. Nobody can act through your connection but you.

Search the catalog in the console, connect an app, and it is yours from the next message. A channel coworker uses the apps it was set up with, so ask an admin to add one with /maia edit.

Connecting takes a minute

There is no admin project and no shared account to set up. Each person connects the apps they use, the same way they would sign in to them.

  1. Find the appSearch the catalog in the console, or wait for Maia to ask.
  2. Sign in onceThe app's own sign-in, with the access you already have.
  3. Maia acts as youFrom the next message, in every channel you use it in.
  4. Disconnect any timeOne click, and every call through that app stops.

What it looks like in a thread

A connection is only useful for what it lets you ask. A few things people ask in the first week.

  • Reply from your inbox

    Draft a reply to a customer from the last three emails and send it from your Gmail, after you approve it.

  • File the bugs from this thread

    Turn a thread of complaints into three issues in Linear or Jira, each with the steps people posted.

  • Pull the numbers before the call

    Ask for this quarter's pipeline from HubSpot or Salesforce, and get it in the thread before the meeting starts.

  • Find the document and the date in it

    Find the Northwind contract in Google Drive and read out the renewal date and the notice period.

If an app is missing, it asks you to connect it

Ask for something that needs an app you have not connected and Maia does not fail. It sends you a private sign-in card, says what it will do next, and waits. Connect the app, say so in the thread, and it carries on. It can answer the parts that did not need the app in the same reply.

Reads run free. Risky writes wait.

Looking something up in an app runs straight through. Sending an email, creating an issue or changing a record goes through a risk gate and your workspace policy, and anything risky raises an approval card first.

Your admin can set a policy per app or per action: always allow, always ask, or block it outright. When a coworker and the workspace disagree, the stricter rule wins.

A read
  1. You askWhich invoices are past due?
  2. Maia looks it upIn the app, with your access.
  3. Answer in the threadNo card, no wait.
A write
  1. You askSend Northwind the renewal.
  2. Maia drafts itAnd shows you the action before it runs.
  3. Approval cardYou, or a named approver, say yes.
  4. Done, loggedThe result posts in the thread. The approval is on the record.

It searches the web and shows its sources

When the answer is not in your apps, Maia searches the web, reads the one or two pages that matter, and gives the link for anything it states from them. Web pages are treated as data, never as instructions.

Each coworker reaches only what it is given

A coworker is set up with the apps it may use. A channel with contractors gets an agent that reaches only what that channel needs. Change the list with /maia edit in the channel. The console shows it read-only.

Under your control

Every connection is personal. Nobody, admin or not, can act through yours. Disconnect an app in the console and every call through it stops at once.

Your admin sets policy per app or per action, always allow, always ask, or block it outright, and the stricter rule wins. Every call an app receives is logged with who asked, what ran and who approved.
